gaps.lead: He can't be in Spain — I saw him here this morning.
gaps.sentence: He ___ in Spain — I saw him this morning.
gaps.explanation: can't/cannot possibly be = it is impossible that he is.

gaps.lead: He spoke slowly because he wanted us to understand him.
gaps.explanation: so that + subject + would/could expresses purpose.

gaps.lead: The concert was cancelled because hardly anybody came.
gaps.sentence: The concert was cancelled ___ people came.
gaps.explanation: because so few people came = because hardly anybody came.

gaps.lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
gaps.explanation: should(n't) have + participle criticises a past decision.

gaps.lead: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have become a famous art historian.
gaps.sentence: If Marc hadn't taken up politics, he might have ___ himself as an art historian.
gaps.hint: become famous = make a ___ for oneself
gaps.explanation: 'Make a name for himself' means become well known.
